## Overview

The Skallfang Clan are the northern barbarian tribe of Kythoria — monster hunters from the frozen northern frontier where civilized lands gradually give way to vast frozen wilderness and the deadliest monster-infested territories. They fought in the First Alliance and were entrusted with guarding Khar'Zul's sealed blade after his defeat. The Skallfang do not attempt to completely tame the northern wilderness — they have learned to live alongside it. Their territory is a constant border between civilization and the monstrous lands beyond.

---

## Territory

The Skallfang settlements are scattered throughout the northern frontier rather than concentrated in a single great city. Their primary strongholds are built around defensible positions, hunting grounds, mountain passes, and ancient monster trails. Their largest settlement serves as the heart of the Clan: **Ulfrheim**, where warriors gather, young hunters train, elders preserve their history, and the current leader holds council.

---

## Culture

The Skallfang are a northern warrior culture shaped by generations of surviving against monsters. Despite their reputation as fierce warriors, they are not simply barbarians — their society values discipline, community, knowledge of the wilderness, and the ability to understand the creatures they hunt. A Skallfang warrior is expected to know more than how to swing a weapon. They must know how to track monsters, identify their weaknesses, survive harsh environments, protect their companions, recognize monster territories, understand signs of an approaching threat, and know when fighting is necessary and when survival requires retreat.

The Clan considers experience one of the greatest forms of knowledge. The oldest hunters are therefore not simply respected because of their age, but because of everything they have survived.

---

## Philosophy

The Skallfang believe that strength has meaning only when it is used to protect others. They do not seek glory through monster hunting; a monster killed in the wilderness is simply one less threat reaching a village. Their greatest victories are often the ones that nobody remembers: a caravan that arrives safely, a village that never gets attacked, a child who grows up without ever seeing the creature that was killed before it reached their home.

Strength is not measured by what you can destroy, but by what you refuse to let be destroyed. This philosophy is particularly important to Balor's upbringing and is one of the reasons Hrothgar's teachings remain fundamental to him.

---

## The Three Oaths

> **WHEN DARKNESS COMES... WE STAND**
> **WHEN DARKNESS GROWS... WE HUNT**
> **WHEN DARKNESS FALLS... WE REMAIN**

---

## The Trial of the Fang

Every Skallfang warrior must eventually undergo The Trial of the Fang. The Trial marks the transition from youth into a true warrior of the Skallfang. Alone, each initiate is sent into the frozen wilderness to overcome a challenge worthy of remembrance. Some return after slaying a great beast. Others survive impossible odds or rescue that which was thought to be lost. They are sent into a path of fate, decided only by the gods — but the deed itself is never what matters most. It is the strength of character revealed through it.

After completing the trial, the warrior receives a byname — a name earned through their actions. Balor received: **The Tainted.**

---

## Attitude

Skallfang tend to be direct, reserved around strangers, fiercely loyal, suspicious of outsiders, practical, resilient, protective, and deeply respectful of experience. They generally dislike unnecessary displays of wealth or status. A nobleman who has never faced a monster has little authority in the eyes of a Skallfang hunter. An old hunter who has saved dozens of lives may command the respect of the entire clan.

---

## Most Common Classes

- Barbarians
- Rangers
- Fighters
- Clerics

---

## Weapons & Equipment

Skallfang equipment is designed around survival and practicality. Their weapons tend to favor axes, spears, great weapons, bows, hunting knives, shields, and weapons specifically adapted to fighting large monsters. Armor is generally practical rather than decorative. Fur, leather, metal plates, and monster components are commonly incorporated into their equipment. A particularly accomplished hunter may carry pieces of a creature they defeated — not purely as trophies, but as reminders of what they survived.

---

## Relationship with Monsters

The Skallfang understand something that many civilized people do not: not every monster behaves the same way. They study creatures and learn their habits, territories, hunting patterns, and weaknesses. Some monsters are immediately hostile; others can be avoided. Some may even coexist with settlements if properly understood. This knowledge makes the Skallfang particularly effective against intelligent or highly territorial creatures. They do not fight monsters simply because they are monsters — they fight them when they represent a threat.

---

## Structure

The clan is organized around its elders, warriors, and hunters. Leadership is earned through skill, courage, and wisdom rather than bloodline. The clan's traditions emphasize honor, duty, and the burden of their sacred trust.

### Keepers of the Oath

The Keepers of the Oath are a specific lineage within the Skallfang Clan, chosen to serve as the blade's direct guardians. Each Keeper serves for life, and the role passes either by inheritance or by proving worth in the Trial of the Fang.

Known Keepers:
- **Hjalvar Skallfang** (current) — Son of Hrothgar. Inherited the mantle after his father's death.
- **Hrothgar Skallfang** (deceased) — The most recent Keeper. Raised Balor and spent decades studying the blade's behavior.
- **Skalda Frost-Beard** — Hrothgar's predecessor, who was the first to document the blade's transformation from steel to flesh. She died of old age.
- **Ragnulf Skallfang** — Ancestor from the First Alliance era. Chieftain who fought Khar'Zul as one of the seven Alliance heroes and was entrusted with guarding the sealed blade after the war.

---

## Current Status

The current chieftain is **Hjalvar Skallfang**, son of Hrothgar. He grew up alongside Balor in Ulfrheim, and throughout their childhood the two became the closest thing either would have to brothers. When Hrothgar died during the attack on Ulfrheim, Hjalvar inherited the mantle of Chieftain.

The clan is now fractured. After the village was destroyed and Balor was found unconscious amidst the ruins, the clan elders made the painful decision to exile him. They knew the truth about his origins — that he was the culmination of Project Genesis — and feared that keeping him would bring destruction upon what remained of the clan.

Despite everything, Hjalvar never came to see Balor as an enemy. Their paths simply became different. As Chief, Hjalvar carries the responsibility of protecting the Skallfang and preserving everything his father spent his life building.
